product_overview: ProctorLess is a privacy-first smart assessment platform designed for university professors and students to conduct online exams with integrity monitoring, AI-assisted grading, and seamless quiz management, reducing stress and manual workload while respecting privacy.
core_goals: Enable university professors to create and manage courses and quizzes easily in one unified platform.
Provide students with a straightforward, non-invasive quiz-taking experience focusing on privacy and fairness.
Implement a privacy-respecting integrity monitor that tracks tab switches without invasive methods like webcams.
Offer AI-assisted grading tools to significantly reduce professors' manual grading time.
Ensure a clean, minimal, and academic UI/UX that builds trust and clarity for all users.
Enable role-based user access distinguishing between professors and students.
Support real-time logging and review of student quiz integrity data and grading results.
key_features: User Authentication and Role Assignment allowing Professors and Students to securely log in and access role-specific dashboards.
Course Management enabling professors to create courses and distribute unique join codes for student enrollment.
Quiz Creation Form with options to upload question banks, enable integrity monitoring, allowlist permitted websites, and toggle AI-assisted grading.
Student Quiz Engine displaying randomized questions from the uploaded bank, supporting multiple-choice and essay answers, with autosave and submission functions.
Privacy-First Integrity Monitoring to detect and log tab switches unless on allowed websites, capturing timestamps and linking data to the student and quiz.
AI-Assisted Grading via a button on the Results page, invoking a Supabase Edge Function connected to Gemini AI for real-time grade and feedback suggestions with manual override capabilities.
Results and Integrity Log Dashboard allowing professors to view quiz grades and detailed tab-switch logs per student.
user_flow_summary: Professor logs in and accesses the main dashboard listing courses.
Professor creates a new course and obtains a unique join code.
Professor initiates quiz creation via a form, setting title, uploading question bank, and configuring integrity monitoring, allowed websites, and AI grading options.
Students log in, join courses by entering the join code, and see quizzes to take.
Student opens a quiz, views rules, completes randomized questions, and submits answers.
Tab switches by the student during a quiz are detected and logged excluding allowed sites.
Professor reviews results on the dashboard, inspects integrity logs for suspicious behavior, and uses the AI-assisted grading button to expedite essay grading.
validation_criteria: Users can sign up and log in with assigned roles; professors and students access respective dashboards correctly.
Professors can create courses that generate unique join codes; students use codes to join courses successfully.
The quiz creation form accepts question bank files, respects form inputs for monitors and allowed sites, and saves quizzes properly.
Students see randomized quiz questions and can answer and submit multiple-choice and essay types with autosave functioning.
Integrity Monitor logs all tab switches with correct metadata except when the student visits allowed URLs.
AI grading button calls a Supabase Edge Function that interacts with the live Gemini AI API and returns grade suggestions visible to the professor.
Results dashboard lists student submissions, grades, and detailed integrity logs accessible by clicking student names.
The entire end-to-end flow — professor creating course/quiz, student taking and submitting quiz, and professor reviewing results with AI grading — works seamlessly on desktop browsers.
The system is deployed and tested with no critical bugs blocking a demo presentation.
